//ConnectionStrings: This file is committed, so it holds a credential-free local default only. The hosted
database's connection string - which carries a password - is supplied by the environment:
locally, appsettings.Development.json (gitignored) overrides it the same way.
//Authentication: Bearer JWTs for both human logins (SEC-32 auth v1) and the ingest endpoint's machine token. Never put the signing key in this file - it is committed. Use user-secrets, environment variables, or appsettings.Development.json.

Jwt.//AccessTokenMinutes: How long an issued access token is valid for.
Jwt.//RefreshTokenDays: How long an issued refresh token is valid for before it must be used or the user logs in again.

//KeyVault: SEC-35 (audit 35-A) - secrets from Azure Key Vault, layered over this file so the vault wins.
Uri empty means no vault: no client, no credential, no network. That is how every test, the
offline demo and a fresh clone run, and it is the default on purpose.
Authentication is DefaultAzureCredential - the Container App's managed identity in Azure,
your own 'az login' locally. There is no client secret to store, which is the point.
Secret names follow the standard double-hyphen convention (Authentication--Jwt--SigningKey
becomes Authentication:Jwt:SigningKey). SecretNames maps the ones that do not: this vault's
secrets predate the convention and are named sql-default-connection, nim-red-key and so on.
Renaming live secrets has an outage in it; declaring the mapping does not.
ReloadIntervalMinutes 0 reads the vault once at startup. See docs/Key_Vault.md.
//BundleStorage: Job-scoped directory where uploaded scan bundles land before the pipeline reads them; purged after the audit (SEC-29).
//Scanning: SEC-46 - the in-process worker that drives queued scan jobs through Pipeline B.
Turn Enabled off on an API instance that should serve requests without running scans;
the claim is safe against concurrent workers, so several instances may leave it on.
//Corpus: Placeholder until Pipeline A publishes a real corpus version (see ConfiguredCorpusVersionProvider).
//Observability: SEC-36 - LLM tracing. OtlpEndpoint empty means tracing is off entirely: no exporter is
registered, no listener subscribes, and the instrumentation costs one null check per turn.
Langfuse Cloud is https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces (or the us. host).
CaptureContent is separate and defaults false. Off, a trace carries tokens, tier, latency
and outcome - nothing of the customer's. On, it also carries the prompts and the answers,
which is what makes a debate replayable AND makes the collector a second destination for
job content beside the model provider. Turning it on therefore requires the collector's
host in Security:Egress:TelemetryHosts, or the deployment stops accepting scan jobs.
Langfuse keys are credentials - supply SecretKey from the environment or Key Vault, never
//Knowledge: The Qdrant corpus Pipeline A produced (SEC-22). Endpoint is the gRPC port, 6334 - the .NET client does not speak the 6333 REST port. Embedder BaseUrl empty means no embedder: the exact-filter arm still grounds every finding with a clean CVE or CWE. See docs/Retrieval.md.

Models.//: Never put API keys in this file - it is committed. Use user-secrets, environment variables, or appsettings.Development.json.
Models.//Provider: Scripted by default so a fresh clone runs with no credentials. Override to Nim in appsettings.Development.json for a live debate.
//Pricing: SEC-31 - what a token costs, per tier, in money per MILLION tokens.
Left empty on purpose: published list prices for Azure, Anthropic and Scripted are
built in and used when nothing is set here. Set a tier to override it - negotiated
rates, a repriced model, or a provider with no list price (NIM), whose tokens are
otherwise counted and reported as unpriced rather than as free.
